news.title: Prince Pipes and Fittings Limited (NSEI:PRINCEPIPE) has completed the acquisition of  Aquel brand and assets of Klaus Waren Fixtures Private Limited from Klaus Waren Fixtures Private Limited and Narshi Mulji Shah for INR 550 million.
news.body:
Prince Pipes and Fittings Limited (NSEI:PRINCEPIPE) has signed an asset purchase agreement to acquire Aquel brand and assets of Klaus Waren Fixtures Private Limited from Klaus Waren Fixtures Private Limited and Narshi Mulji Shah for INR 550 million on March 20, 2024. The board of Prince Pipes and Fittings Limited has approved the transaction. The acquisition is subject to approval of Collector Office, Revenue Branch, Bhuj, Gujarat. The acquisition is to be done in two tranches in which the first tranche of the acquisition of the relevant assets is to be completed within 10 days from execution of agreement and the second tranche of the acquisition of the relevant assets to be completed by October 15, 2024. The acquisition is funded through internal accruals.

news.title: Now 21% undervalued after recent price drop
news.body: Over the last 90 days, the stock has fallen 15% to ₹266. The fair value is estimated to be ₹335, however this is not to be taken as a buy recommendation but rather should be used as a guide only. Revenue has declined by 3.9% over the last 3 years. Earnings per share has declined by 41%. Revenue is forecast to grow by 29% in 2 years. Earnings are forecast to grow by 240% in the next 2 years.

news.title: Price target decreased by 10% to ₹308
news.body: Down from ₹344, the current price target is an average from 13 analysts. New target price is 13% above last closing price of ₹272. Stock is down 5.3% over the past year. The company is forecast to post earnings per share of ₹4.23 for next year compared to ₹3.90 last year.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: ₹0.21 loss per share (vs ₹1.85 loss in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: ₹0.21 loss per share (improved from ₹1.85 loss in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹5.75b (flat on 3Q 2025). Net loss: ₹3.27m (loss narrowed 98% from 3Q 2025). Revenue is forecast to grow 13% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 14% growth forecast for the Building industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 42% per year but the company’s share price has only fallen by 22% per year, which means it has not declined as severely as earnings.
